Metric correctly awards 0.2 for the 'Net Income' header and 0.8 distributed across 19 rows (~0.042 each), providing meaningful partial credit.
Expected values are hardcoded and consistent with the evaluator.expected.rules section, representing Revenue - Total Expenses per row.
Negative control resistance is adequate: the initial file has no column C data, so the initial state will score ~0 and not pass.
Float-to-int normalization is applied in both getter and metric, preventing false negatives when LibreOffice stores integer values as floats.
